personas.name: routine-rhinitis-aeroallergen-skin-prick-complete
personas.description: Well-formed routine GP referral: perennial rhinitis, aeroallergen skin-prick testing requested (first-line), no antihistamines / skin disease / beta-blocker concerns, every completeness field present — expect usually-appropriate + ok + routine + accept.

indication.clinicalQuestion: Perennial nasal congestion and sneezing worse indoors — assess for house dust mite / animal dander sensitisation.
indication.clinicalDetails: Symptoms year-round, worse at home; two cats in the household. No asthma diagnosis.

triage.notes: Patient to stop antihistamines 5 days before the appointment (advice already given).

firedRules.description: Requested skin-prick-test is the recommended test for "rhinitis-asthma".

personas.name: urgent-venom-allergy-beta-blocker-anaphylaxis-caution
personas.description: Systemic reaction to a wasp sting with a background of previous anaphylaxis and current beta-blocker therapy — venom skin-prick testing is first-line and the indication itself auto-escalates triage to urgent, but the beta-blocker + anaphylaxis-history combination forces a safety caution (adrenaline may be less effective if a systemic reaction occurs during testing) — expect usually-appropriate + caution + urgent + accept (this engine only redirects on the contraindicated band, not caution).

indication.clinicalQuestion: Generalised urticaria, facial swelling, and hypotension within 15 minutes of a wasp sting last month, treated with IM adrenaline — assess for venom sensitisation ahead of immunotherapy.
indication.clinicalDetails: Beta-blocker (bisoprolol) for hypertension. Carries two adrenaline auto-injectors.

triage.notes: Testing to be performed in a resuscitation-ready setting with senior cover.

firedRules.description: Requested skin-prick-test is the recommended test for "venom-allergy".
Beta-blocker with a history of anaphylaxis — adrenaline may be less effective if a systemic reaction occurs during testing.
History of anaphylaxis — expedite assessment in a resuscitation-ready setting.
Venom allergy with systemic-reaction risk — expedite testing and immunotherapy assessment.

flags.description: Patient has a history of anaphylaxis.
flags.suggestedAction: Perform testing in a resuscitation-ready setting with adrenaline and trained staff immediately available.

flags.description: Beta-blocker with a history of anaphylaxis — adrenaline may be less effective.
flags.suggestedAction: Review whether the beta-blocker can be safely withheld; ensure resuscitation readiness before any provocation or skin testing.

personas.name: invalidated-food-allergy-antihistamines-incomplete
personas.description: Suspected peanut allergy referred from primary care: skin-prick testing is first-line, but the patient is still taking daily antihistamines, which invalidates the weal-and-flare response — the test cannot proceed until an appropriate washout — and several administrative fields were left blank on the referral form — expect usually-appropriate + contraindicated + routine + redirect (not reject — this engine redirects patients to a washout / alternative test rather than rejecting outright), completeness below 100.

indication.clinicalDetails: Facial rash and lip swelling after eating a peanut-containing snack. On daily cetirizine for eczema.

triage.notes: Parent not advised to stop antihistamines before referral was submitted.

expected.recommendationLabel: Redirect to a more suitable test

flags.description: Patient is on antihistamines — skin-prick / intradermal testing will be invalid.
flags.suggestedAction: Stop antihistamines for an appropriate washout (typically five half-lives) before testing, or use specific-IgE blood testing instead.
